caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 422 of 2010
lawyer:
Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner
Syed Mahbubur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Principal and Secretary, Nawabgonj Government College, Nawabgonj ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Mahabuba Khatun (Dolly) and others ------ Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and Order dated 21.07.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 358 of 2002)
full_judgment:
Nazmun Ara Sultana, J. <u>This Civil Petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 21.07.2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 358 of 2002 allowing the appeal and reversing the judgment and decree dated 05.02.2002 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Nawabgonj in Other Class Suit No. 57 of 1987 dismissing the suit. The plaintiff-respondent herein filed the above mentioned Other Class Suit No. 57 of 1987 for declaration of title and partition. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that 4.02 acres of land as described in schedule 'Ka' to the plaint originally belonged to 3 brothers, namely, Ashutosh Chatyapadhya, Sharat Chandra Chatyapadhya and Monimdra Chatyapadhya in equal share and the C.S. Khatian was accordingly prepared in their names. That after partition of Pakistan and India Sharat Chandra Migrated to India and arranged an exchange of his share i.e. .95 acre out of schedule 'Ka' land with Indian land of one Ishahaque Mia-the father of the plaintiffs. That for effecting the exchange Sharat Chandra executed a power of attorney in favour of one Harun-ar-Rashid. Harun-ar-Rashid having obtained necessary permission from the then District Collector, Rajshahi, executed and registered a deed of exchange dated 13.10.1952 in favour of Ishahaque Mia. Thus Ishahaque Mia having acquired title and possession in the suit land had been in possession and enjoyment of the same for long 20 years within the knowledge of all including the defendants, Nawabgonj Government College and others. That Ishahaque Mia while in possession of the suit land executed a power of attorney in favour of Harun-ar-Rashid who being so empowered executed and registered two hiba-bil-ewaj deeds dated 09.10.1974 transferring the said .94 acre of land of Ishahaque Mia in favour of his daughters, the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 4. Thus the plaintiffs acquired the suit land and since acquisition they have been in possession of the same by paying rent to the government to the knowledge of all including the defendants. That the defendant college subsequently purchased 2/3rd share of 'Ka' schedule land from Ashutosh and Monindra and has been in ejamali possession of that land with Ishahaque Mia and thereafter with the plaintiffs. That the 'Ka' schedule land has never been partitioned by metes and bounds among these co-sharers. That only in the month of October, 1985 when an employee of the plaintiffs went to pay rent in the local Tahsil Office the Tahsildar disclosed that the land was recorded in the name of the defendant No. 1 College in R.S. Khatian and was finally published. That this R.S. record of the land in the name of the college in 16 annas share is wrong and collusive. That on the basis of this wrong recording the defendant college claimed title in the entire 'Ka' schedule land and thus the title of the plaintiffs in the suit has been clouded and hence the suit.</u>

2. The defendant college and the government contested the suit by filing a joint written statement. These defendants admit the title of 3 C.S. recorded tenants and subsequently also of Ishahaque Mia in the 'Ka' schedule land. But their case is that the defendant college being established in the then newly created Nawabgonj Sub-Division purchased 95 1/2 decimals of land of 'Ka' schedule from Ashutosh Chattapadhya by a registered sale deed dated 23.02.1957 and also purchased the other 95 1/2 decimals of land from Monindra Chatyapadhya Chandra by registered sale deed dated 12.04.1957. That the share of Sharat Chandra was transferred to Ishahaque Mia by way of exchange and the said Ishahaque Mia transferred his 95 1/2 decimals of land to the college by an oral gift in presence of many and the college authority accepted it with gratitude. These defendants stated also that out of 4.02 acres of land described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint 2.86 acres of land only finally stood as rest 1.16 acres fell into road and ditches. That the college authority thus, is in possession of 2.86 acres of land of the 'Ka' schedule to the knowledge of all including the plaintiffs. This land has been duly recorded in the name of the college in R.S. khatian. The college authority has erected wall on the west and northern side of the R.S. plot few years ago. The college authority is in possession of the suit land for more than 12 years and as such they have acquired title by adverse possession also. That the plaintiffs have filed this suit on false claim suppressing the real facts.

3. Before the trial court the plaintiffs examined 7 witnesses and the defendant examined 3 witnesses. The trial court, on consideration of the evidence adduced by the parties, dismissed the suit holding, inter-alia, that the suit land is admittedly in possession of the college and that there is no allegation of forcible dispossession by the college and that the plaintiffs created the hiba-bil-ewaj and sale deeds from a person having no title to the suit land and that too after the same had been in possession by the college for more than twelve years.

4. On appeal the High Court Division set aside the findings and decision of the trial court and decreed the suit making observations and findings to the effect that the plaintiffs being daughters of the admitted co-sharers have succeeded in proving their title to the extent of 1/3rd share in the land described in schedule 'Ka' of the plaint and that the defendants could not prove their claim that the father, of the plaintiffs transferred his 1/3rd share in the 'Ka' schedule land in favour of the defendant college by oral gift and that the defendant college could not prove also its claim that the college has acquired title in this land by adverse possession also and that the recording of the 'Ka' schedule land in the name of the defendant college in 16 annas in R.S. Khatian has been wrong.

5. Mr. Nurul Islam Bhuiyan, the learned Advocate-on-Record for the leave-petitioner-defendant Nawabgonj Government College though has made some submissions in support of the leave-petition, but he could not assail the above findings and decision of the High Court Division.

6. We have gone through the impugned judgment of the High Court Division, that of the trial court and also the evidence on record.

7. We find that the High Court Division, on meticulous examination of the evidence adduced by both the parties, rightly found that the contesting defendants could not prove at all their case that Ishahaque Mia the admitted co-sharer of the 'Ka' schedule land-gifted his 1/3rd share in favour of the defendant college orally. The High Court Division, on consideration of evidence and facts and circumstances and making elaborate discussion found also that the contesting defendants' claim that the defendant college has acquired title in the suit land by virtue of adverse possession also-has not been proved at all.

<u>8. We have gone through the evidence on record. We find nothing to disagree with the above findings and decision of the High Court Division. It is admitted that Ishahaque Mia became the owner of the 1/3rd share of C.S. recorded tenant Sharat Chandra Chatyapadhya by way of exchange and he was also in possession of these 1/3rd share of the schedule 'Ka' land. The plaintiffs are the four daughters of this Ishahaque Mia. The trial court though made some observations that the plaintiffs could not prove their case that they acquired these 1/3rd share of their father by two registered hiba-bil-ewaj deeds, but the High Court Division found that the plaintiffs have proved their title in these 1/3rd share of Ishahaque Mia. The High Court Division rightly made observations to the effect that the plaintiffs though could not produce the original copy of their title deeds, namely, heba-bilewaj deeds and also the power of attorney executed by their father Ishahaque Mia in favour of Harun-ar-Rashid and gave explanations of failure to file those original deeds, but in consideration of the fact that the plaintiffs, being natural heirs of the vendor Ishahaque Mia, had no reason to create those documents in respect of their heritable property for maintaining a partition suit against co-sharer in joint possession. We find these observations of the High Court Division also reasonable. It is in evidence that Ishahaque Mia had four daughters the plaintiffs only, he had no son. Any other distant relation of Ishahaque Mia is not coming to raise any claim in respect of the property of Ishahaque Mia. These facts and circumstances also supports the genuineness of the plaintiffs' title deeds.</u>

9. However, we find that the High Court Division, on careful examination and consideration of the evidence adduced by both the parties and on making elaborate discussion rightly arrived at the decision that in this suit the plaintiffs have successfully proved their title and also possession in 1/3rd share of the schedule 'Ka' land and that the defendants could not prove their case that Ishahaque Mia orally gifted his 1/3rd share in schedule 'Ka' land in favour of the defendant college and also their further case that the defendant college has acquired title in the 1/3rd share of Ishahaque Mia by adverse possession. The impugned judgment of the High Court Division is well reasoned and well written one.

10. We find nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment of the High Court Division.

Hence this Civil Petition for Leave to appeal is dismissed.

End.
